scalars.scalar_value: RECRUITMENT PERIOD ONE MONTH: Applicants will be screened after two weeks; and then on a weekly basis.  The position can be filled prior to the apply by date.
Experience in aseptic technique and circulation in an OR.
Experience to independently provide treatment of patients whose conditions are likely to change on a moment-to-moment basis.

items.item_text: Must possess a California Registered Veterinary Technician (RVT) license or hold a current license in another state and obtain a CA RVT license within 3 months from the date of hire.
Experience to independently provide treatment of patients whose conditions are likely to change on a moment-to-moment basis.
Experience in aseptic technique and circulation in an OR.
Experience calculating drug dosages and administering medications intravenously, subcutaneously, intramuscular or orally.
Experience in a clinical hospital setting with various species performing sedation and anesthesia.

Experience performing venipuncture, placing vascular catheters, inducing anesthesia, monitoring anesthesia, and recovering patients from anesthesia, working independently with and without direct supervision.
Experience in aseptic technique, surgical clipping and patient preparation, and circulation in an O.R.
Experience to recognize normal and abnormal parameters for patients and how to respond accordingly.

Independent of supervision in a hospital setting, as a significant part of daily duties, responsible for treatment of patients with life-threatening illness or injury, whose conditions are likely to change on a moment-to-moment basis and inducing and monitoring anesthesia. Under the direction of the Small Animal Neurology Supervisor and the Neurology/Neurosurgery Service Chief, provide technical support to the Neurology/Neurosurgery service. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to, anesthesia induction and monitoring; surgical preparation for various procedures; operating room circulation; instruction of students and residents in technical skills; patient treatments; diagnostic sample collection; and performing technical procedures such as intravenous catheter placement, blood collection, and urinary catheter placement. Additional responsibilities include client communication and education, patient admission and discharge, and collaboration with colleagues to support team effectiveness and achieve Neurology Service objectives.
Strong interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills to engage effectively with diverse students, staff, clinicians, and clients and the skill to recognize and manage difficult situations.
Ability to recognize peri-anesthetic problems and patient concerns and to effectively communicate problems or concerns to the supervising veterinarian in a timely manner.
Knowledge of normal laboratory values for cats and dogs.
